notes.text: Patrick Kane is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Tyler Bertuzzi has taken his spot beside Connor Bedard and Roman Kantserov.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 33% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 101:32 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Jordan Greenway and Ryan Greene.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 8 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Gage Goncalves takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L3. J.J. Moser is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Crozier and Carlson.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 70% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 25 seconds at a time, against 70 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (24 of 30 changes).

stakes: The Blackhawks go in eighth in the Central with 9 points, the Lightning tied for fourth in the Atlantic with 20 points.

TBL.head: A big edge for the Lightning
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Chicago is on the second night of a back-to-back. If the Blackhawks want to spoil it, start with a penalty kill that holds up.

CHI.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Chicago is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Blackhawks’ best hope is a penalty kill that holds up, plus a big night from Andrei Vasilevskiy.

story.head: Mikheyev meets his old team
paras: The Lightning (9-3-2) beat Detroit 4-2 on Tuesday, while the Blackhawks are winless in four (0-3-1). Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Lightning fourth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.281) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .379, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.714) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blackhawks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Lightning’s penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.25 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.94, the second most. As for the Lightning, they ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd), get into a lot of chippy games (2nd) and take a lot of high-quality shots (4th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.71 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Lightning are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Connor Bedard (4 G / 8 A / 12 P in 10 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Roman Kantserov (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 16 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Lightning, Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Chicago. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Andrei Vasilevskiy (7-3-1 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to start for Chicago, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (7-3-1 / .879 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay.

At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Viel, Geekie and Goncalves out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Smith, Greene and Greenway. Elsewhere, the Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
